parameters.content:
## DEV Video Edit Pipeline (v1)

Skywide-style architecture, inverted cost profile:
**code does the cutting, AI only does the thinking.**

LLM calls per video: 3 small ones
1. Parse Video Brief (structured JSON from free text)
2. Generate EDL (pick in/out points from transcript + silence map)
3. Fix EDL (only fires if validation fails, capped at 2 retries)

Everything else is ffmpeg/ffprobe via Execute Command + Code nodes: probing, silence detection, caption building, cutting, cropping 9:16, loudness normalize, QA.

Est. cost per video: Whisper (~$0.006/min) + 2-3 cheap LLM calls = well under $0.50.

## Setup checklist (before first run)

1. Self-hosted n8n with **ffmpeg + ffprobe** installed on the container/host (`apt-get install ffmpeg`)
2. Attach credentials after import:
   - OpenAI (Parse Brief, Generate EDL, Fix EDL, Whisper Transcribe)
   - Google Drive OAuth (Download, Create Folder, Upload)
3. Replace `YOUR-DASHBOARD.example.com` in Startup Update / Completion Webhook / Send Error nodes (or delete them if no dashboard yet)
4. POST to the webhook:
```json
{
  "title": "My podcast ep 12 clips",
  "video_file_id": "<Google Drive file id>",
  "creative_brief": "Make 3 punchy 60s vertical clips, captions on, keep the story about the client win, cut all rambling",
  "request_id": "...",
  "run_id": "..."
}
```

values.content:
You are a strict extraction agent for a video editing pipeline. Parse the free-form video brief into JSON. Return ONLY valid JSON, no markdown:
{
  "target_clip_seconds": number (default 60),
  "clips_count": number (default 3),
  "aspect_ratio": "9:16" | "16:9" | "1:1" (default "9:16"),
  "captions": boolean (default true),
  "tone": "string describing desired pacing/energy",
  "must_keep_moments": ["topics or quotes the user explicitly wants kept"],
  "global_rules": ["any other directives: no profanity bleeps, keep intros, etc."]
}
Use defaults for anything not specified. Never invent must_keep_moments that were not mentioned.

parameters.command: =bash -c "ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams /tmp/vp_{{ $execution.id }}_source.mp4 > /tmp/vp_{{ $execution.id }}_probe.json; ffmpeg -hide_banner -i /tmp/vp_{{ $execution.id }}_source.mp4 -af silencedetect=noise=-35dB:d=0.5 -f null - 2> /tmp/vp_{{ $execution.id }}_silence.log; ffmpeg -hide_banner -i /tmp/vp_{{ $execution.id }}_source.mp4 -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 -b:a 64k -y /tmp/vp_{{ $execution.id }}_audio.mp3 2>/dev/null; cat /tmp/vp_{{ $execution.id }}_probe.json; echo ---SILENCE---; cat /tmp/vp_{{ $execution.id }}_silence.log"

values.content:
You are an expert short-form video edit planner. You receive a timestamped transcript, a silence map, and an edit brief. You NEVER touch media - you only decide WHAT to cut. Return ONLY valid JSON, no markdown:
{
  "clips": [ { "start": seconds, "end": seconds, "label": "short_slug", "reason": "why this segment works as a clip" } ],
  "video_title": "string",
  "video_description": "string"
}

RULES:
1. Produce exactly clips_count clips, each within +/-15% of target_clip_seconds.
2. Clip boundaries MUST land on transcript segment boundaries - never cut mid-sentence.
3. Prefer boundaries that fall inside or next to silences (the silence map is provided) so cuts feel natural.
4. The strongest hook goes first: pick moments with a clear payoff, story, or bold claim in the first 3 seconds.
5. Every must_keep_moments topic from the brief MUST be covered by at least one clip.
6. Clips must not overlap. start < end for every clip. All timestamps within [0, duration].
7. Respect all global_rules from the brief.

=EDIT CONTEXT (duration, silences, transcript segments, brief):

{{ JSON.stringify($json) }}

You are a surgical EDL fixer. You receive a video edit decision list and a precise list of validation issues. Fix ONLY the listed issues and return the COMPLETE corrected EDL in the exact same JSON schema ({clips:[{start,end,label,reason}],video_title,video_description}). Do not change clips that have no issues. Return ONLY valid JSON.
